title: Replace every use of a word in a memo open in Mousepad, and save it

capabilities.why: Mousepad, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

pick.o2: The colour of the front door stays.
pick.o3: Paint dries fast, so check the colour twice.
pick.n1: Pick a color for the hall.
pick.n2: The color of the front door stays.
pick.n3: Paint dries fast, so check the color twice.

pick.o3: Tuesday lunch is on the team.

setup.why: Write the memo in the run's folder.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec mousepad /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/memo-{{nonce}}.txt

setup.why: Wait for Mousepad's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, and put the pointer on it: with no window manager, keys go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class mousepad | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Mousepad window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); sleep 1

instruction: Mousepad has memo-{{nonce}}.txt open. Replace every "{{w.old}}" in it with "{{w.new}}", change nothing else, and save the file. This desktop has no window manager: keys go to the window under the mouse pointer.

checks.why: The saved memo holds its four lines with all three uses of "{{w.old}}" replaced and nothing else changed (leading and trailing blank space aside). Setup wrote the old word, so an agent that does nothing fails, and so does one that replaces only some.

teardown.why: Close Mousepad without saving (KILL: Mousepad holds on to a changed document on TERM) and delete the run's folder.

oracle.why: Select all (Ctrl+A) and type the memo back with the word replaced, then Save (Ctrl+S): the file has a name, so no dialog.
